description: This Canada1Water release provides hydraulic-property rasters for the fifty-to-one-hundred-centimetre soil layer across continental Canada and shared United States watersheds. The producers combined depth-averaged OpenLandMap mineral-soil variables with Rosetta v3 pedotransfer estimates, then assigned bedrock and peatland hydraulic classes for continental hydrological modelling. The article describes water-retention parameters and saturated hydraulic conductivity among the 18 bands. Zenodo lists 57 ten-degree GeoTIFF macrotiles and five accompanying style or documentation files, all public under CC BY 4.0. The lower layer has its own DOI and differs from the separately deposited zero-to-fifty-centimetre layer in depth and bedrock extent. Coverage is mapped hydraulic parameters, not direct subsurface observations or validated predictions at every tile. Input-map uncertainty, vertical averaging, bedrock masks and assumed peat classes are limitations for local recharge or runoff interpretation. A reviewer-assessed use is supplying the second near-surface layer in groundwater and surface-water simulations. model-wflow is a related hydrological modelling resource, and data-isric-soilgrids-global-soil-maps is another global soil product; direct parameter mapping was not tested. No GeoTIFF or ZIP file was downloaded or analysed.
